catalog_quote: Stress is phonemic in Nuaulu but it carries a light functional load. Primary stress generally occurs on the penultimate syllable of a bisyllabic word-root and does not shift with the addition or deletion of affixes. Thus, if a single-syllable suffix is added to the root of such a word, stress would be on the ante-penultimate syllable. ['rana] /rana/ 'grate/parut' [ka-'rana-te] /ka-rana-te/ 'grater/parutan' ... Words with a root of four or more syllables have secondary stress (") on the first syllable in addition to primary stress (') on the penultimate syllable of the root. ... 3.3.1 Discrepancies to Stress Rule There are three types of discrepancies to the above stress rule. The first of these is words having a one syllable root such as /sa/ 'climb/naik', where there is, of course, no penultimate syllable on which stress could occur. audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding quotation, the dq and the exception quote are all verbatim on printed pp.102-103 (PDF pp.111-112) of the held WILC vol.7 scan, exactly as the locator says; I read the rendered page image, not just the scanned. (2) The classification rests on a primary, fieldwork-based phonology article (Bolton 1989, SIL/Pattimura WILC 7) with an explicit stress section whose wording directly supports 'morphological' (root-penult, stress does not shift under prefixation or suffixation, surface antepenult with monosyllabic suffixes, contrastive pairs from affixation, secondary stress root-initial in 4+ syllable roots, listed lexical exceptions). Glottolog's descriptive bibliography has only two items, both by Bolton; the unheld one is her 1990 M.A. thesis, not available online per the SIL archive record fetched sources now. Crossref and Semantic Scholar queries

sources.note: The only other descriptive work on Nuaulu and the only grammar-length one (Glottolog hhtype 'grammar'); same author as our deciding 1989 phonology article, so it would confirm whether the root-domain penult rule and the affix behaviour ([ka-'rana-te], [o-'sa] vs ['osa]) are stated identically with fuller morphology (which prefixes/suffixes, clitics vs affixes) — useful for the prule's 'prefixes AND suffixes' claim and the exception list.
